title: Article 89 — The Chairman and Deputy Chairman of the Council of States

content.overview: Article 89 provides that the Vice-President of India shall be ex officio Chairman of the Council of States, and that the Council shall choose a Deputy Chairman from among its members as soon as may be.
content.glance: Vice-President = ex officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha. Council chooses a Deputy Chairman from its members.
content.study:
Article 89:
(1) The Vice-President of India shall be ex officio Chairman of the Council of States.
(2) The Council of States shall, as soon as may be, choose a member of the Council to be Deputy Chairman thereof and, so often as the office of Deputy Chairman becomes vacant, the Council shall choose another member to be Deputy Chairman thereof.

Related: Arts 90–92 (vacation, resignation, removal, performance of duties of Chairman).

Examination: Vice-President is Chairman by virtue of office; Deputy Chairman is elected from among members.

sections.heading: Key points
sections.body:
- Chairman: Vice-President (ex officio).
- Deputy Chairman: chosen by the Council from its members; vacancy filled by fresh choice.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Who is the Chairman of the Council of States?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 89, the Vice-President of India is the ex officio Chairman of the Council of States. The Council chooses a Deputy Chairman from among its members.

examTips: Vice-President = ex officio Chairman of RS.

keyTakeaways: VP is ex officio Chairman of Rajya Sabha; Deputy Chairman elected from members.
